podcast.title: Anthem for Birth Control
podcast.body: This song, written by Lorraine Allen, Don McCann, and T.D. Bayless, and produced by country music legend Owen Bradley, was recorded in 1972 but not released by Loretta's record label until 1975. The lyrics celebrate the freedom offered by the birth control pill, with the singer expressing joy at no longer being a "baby making machine" and being able to have sex for fun. Its progressive message about female sexual autonomy was considered "distasteful" by some radio stations in 1975, yet it became a reflection of the importance of the pill in both the sexual revolution and the women's rights movement. "In 1972 she recorded the song The Pill, which was written by Lorraine Allen, Don McCann, and T.D. Bayless."

Released in 1975, "The Pill" was so controversial that radio stations refused to play it, as a song explicitly about birth control was considered too provocative at the time. "Radio stations would not even play the pill in 1975 because a song about birth control was just too controversial."
